commits.message:
test(fault-proofs): drop the wasm heap guard now that both leaks are fixed

tests/support/uplc-heap-guard.ts existed for two leaks in the pinned
lucid-evolution packages: a forced garbage collection after each test to
release finalizer-managed CML objects, and a wasm32-ceiling check for the
uplc allocator that never reclaimed linear memory. lucid 0.6.4 and uplc
0.2.23 fix both upstream, so the guard, its setup-file entry, and the
--expose-gc flag in the shared fork pool go. Per-file process isolation
stays: wasm linear memory never shrinks, and a fresh process per file is
what hands it back.

The test files that justified their one-journey-per-file split with the
leak now record that the leak is fixed and the split is kept for that
isolation; no files were merged. Full suite on the new packages: 219 s,
same failure set as before the change.

build(demo): bump lucid-evolution to lucid 0.6.4 and uplc 0.2.23

lucid 0.6.4 (with core-utils 0.1.17, utils 0.1.74, plutus 0.1.36,
provider 0.2.3, wallet 0.2.2) frees cardano-multiplatform-lib objects
explicitly instead of leaving them to wasm-bindgen's finalizer, and uplc
0.2.23 drops the wee_alloc allocator that never reused a freed block.
Together they remove the two wasm memory leaks that made the emulator
suites' last tests spend minutes in garbage collection.

fix(cek): make map conversions agree across builder, verifiers and core

`mapData`/`unMapData` (builtin tags 38/43) disagreed between the trace
builder, the TypeScript step verifier and the core program-material
verifier, so the golden channel could only pin the four map-conversion
arms from a ~9 KB script context.

The L1 rule (PlutusCore.Data and builtinCostModelC) is the reference:
both builtins are constant-cost and total for any width including the
empty map, `unMapData` fails only on a non-Map, and Data maps are
CBOR-encoded with a definite map header.

- midgard-core `cek-proof.ts` committed and verified Data map nodes with
  the list CBOR-length rule (indefinite `2 + payload`) instead of the
  definite map header, so any program carrying an inline map constant
  failed material verification ("CEK Data map summary is invalid").
  Aiken `map_cbor_length` and validation's `cek-data-tree.ts` already
  applied the map rule.
- `verifyMapConversionStart` only accepted `semanticConstant` witnesses,
  while Aiken `semantic_constant_parts_v1` accepts an inline
  `ConstantValue` too, so every result at or below the inline bound was
  refused. It now resolves both endpoints through `constantParts` like
  the other semantic arms.
- The builder routes tags 38/43 through the map-conversion micro-machine
  for inline and semantic sources alike; `unMapData` on a non-map inline
  constant takes the semantic-failure arm like tags 42 and 44-46.

Golden channel: four new programs (narrow, empty, inline-constant and
inline wrong-variant map conversions); 26 programs, 403 steps, 132 Aiken
tests, `--check` byte-stable.

test(cek): add the V1 core-step cross-language golden channel

The Aiken CEK verifier and the TypeScript CEK trace builder and step verifier
were pinned against each other by nine mode tags, eight error tags, and one
hand-pasted CBOR vector; nothing proved that a step the TypeScript builder
emits is a step verify_core_step_v1 accepts.

Add a generator on the existing golden-channel pattern that executes
twenty-two curated programs through the TypeScript builder and emits, per
program, the script bytes, context CBOR, envelope and application roots, the
initial and terminal state hashes, every step's CoreStepEvidenceV1 CBOR with
its pre/post state hashes, the stop reason, and two negative twists. The
vitest suite replays every step through the TypeScript verifier and the
generated Aiken module deserialises each pinned CBOR, re-serialises it
byte-for-byte, recomputes both state hashes, and runs verify_core_step_v1,
with the twists pinned as refusals. All forty-one witness arms are reached
and both consumers fail if that coverage shrinks. The `--check` script joins
the CI job beside the sibling fixture checks so an edited producer plus a
`:sync` cannot re-green both suites unnoticed.

refactor(da): hoist the libp2p identity loader into midgard-core

midgard-node and da-committee-node each carried their own copy of the
DA_LIBP2P_PRIVATE_KEY_SOURCE loader (seed:, hex:, and file: schemes), and
the two had drifted in validation and error wording, so a source accepted by
one side of the DA transport could be rejected by the other. Move it to
@al-ft/midgard-core/da-libp2p-identity with one definition of the grammar,
hex validation through the core hexToBytes helper, and a test that pins seed
spelling invariance, the hex:/file: round-trip of the protobuf key, and the
rejections, then point both packages and their tests at the shared module.

build(watcher): declare @noble/hashes instead of reaching into midgard-core's node_modules

Eight watcher modules imported blake2b through a relative
`../../../midgard-core/node_modules/@noble/hashes` path, which only resolved
because pnpm happened to lay the sibling package's store out next door and
would break on any hoisting or install-layout change. Add @noble/hashes to
the watcher's own dependencies and import it by package name.

fix(watcher): route every canonical-JSON digest through the hardened durable-store walk

The settlement indexer carried its own canonical-JSON walk with no number
branch, so any number reaching it serialized as `{}` before sha256 and
before the `same()` equality the indexer uses at thirty-six sites: two
states differing only in a numeric field hashed and compared as identical.
The state-queue and proof-thread indexers, the L1 adapter, the funding
overlay, and three test files each carried a further private copy of the
walk with their own divergent handling.

Delete all of them and alias the indexers' sha256Canonical/same helpers and
the encoders onto watcherCanonicalJson, watcherSha256CanonicalJson, and
watcherSameCanonicalJson from durable-store, whose walk carries safe
integers verbatim, rejects unsafe numbers, sparse arrays, non-plain records,
accessors, and cycles, and sorts keys in the same code-unit order the removed
copies used, so every existing digest is byte-stable. The test support module
now wraps the production walk instead of restating it, and the settlement
suite pins that the state and result encoders emit the durable-store bytes
and that numerically distinct values no longer collapse to one digest.

refactor(demo): share test support, ratchet no-unsafe lint, and dedupe environment reads

Add the private @al-ft/midgard-test-support workspace package so the
vitest config helpers (isolated forks pool, midgard-source SSR resolution,
raw SQL loader), the temp-file helpers previously copied between midgard-node
and midgard-node-tools, and the h28/h32/ordinalHex fixture helpers that every
suite restated live in one place.

Add midgard-core narrowing, lucid-data, and canonical-json modules and a
plutus-data-narrowing module in midgard-validation, then turn the
@typescript-eslint no-unsafe-* rules back on for midgard-core and
midgard-validation. The `Schema as unknown as Type` Lucid data casts across
midgard-sdk, midgard-fault-proofs, midgard-watcher, and midgard-node become
asDataType<Type>(Schema), which states the one honest cast once.

Give midgard-node and midgard-node-tools an environment module that holds
the single definition of each directly read variable (the DA availability
block, deployment manifest and blueprint overrides, bond-owner credential,
economics profile), replacing the near-copies scattered through commands,
fibers, and blueprint loaders. Drop the node's prebuild script, which
rebuilt sibling packages the workspace already builds.

Wire the network-id forced step into the SDK chain builder and carry it on
the fault-proofs emulator scaffold, teach the reference-script publisher the
chains whose contract names are not Step{n+1} so a lettered or appended step
can no longer publish one family member's script under another's role, parse
the state-queue yield validators and withdraw purpose in the DA committee
deployment reader, memoize the watcher's positional contract script hashes,
and extend the fault-proofs heap guard to reclaim the CML arena between
emulator journeys.

fix(onchain): derive the CEK program-material bound from the 447-byte V1 DA framing

The TypeScript twin has pinned MIDGARD_CEK_PROGRAM_MATERIAL_DA_FIXED_BYTES at
447 since the sdk da-payload suite started measuring the framing against the
canonical encoder, while cek-proof-v1.ak still derived
max_program_material_byte_length from 446 and so admitted 67108418 material
bytes where the consensus profile allows 67108417.

Align the Aiken constant and the two suites that pin hashes derived from it,
republish the consensus profile document and its digest, the format registry
entry, and the DA committee deployment fixture, and make the core profile
tests read the bound from MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS instead of restating the
stale literal.

refactor(fault-proofs): remove the family-scaffold generator

The scaffold-family command and its src/family-scaffold generator were a
one-shot boilerplate tool that no shipped fault-proof family was produced
by or depends on. Every family in the tree was written by hand against the
shipped shapes, and the generator had already drifted from them once
(f3b03c91d re-derived it onto the post-#575 vocabularies after it emitted
three retired ones), so keeping it meant maintaining a second copy of the
family layout that nothing exercised. The per-family duplication it papered
over is being removed separately by making family steps table-driven, so
the generator, its layout-enforcing test, and its example spec go first.

Removed: src/family-scaffold/ (spec, emit, generate, permissive-dispatch),
tests/family-scaffold.test.ts, the templates/ example spec, the
scaffold-family verb with its --scaffold-spec/--repo-root/--dry-run flags
and usage line in bin.ts, and the package-root re-export. The docs-site
CLI overview drops the Scaffold group and its command count follows the
usage template; the Aiken native-binding fixture keeps its enumerated-arm
comments without the generator-rule attribution.

GOAL_SPEC Q02 no longer names the generator; it now states the three
properties that survive the deletion: each family declares its step datum
and redeemer schemas as concrete typed values in its own module, dispatch
is a typed map over a closed category union with no default arm, and each
family has its own emulator-driven test.

chore(repo): restore the offchain Haskell operator-directory library

`offchain/` is the Haskell/Cabal package that builds the operator-directory
transactions (active, registered, and retired operator lists, the scheduler,
and initialisation) with its own specs. It was retired in 81a511e15 as a
dormant scaffold; it is a working library, so it comes back exactly as it was,
with its docs-site page, navigation entry, and repository-map row.

The root `.pre-commit-config.yaml` symlink stays: it is the git-hooks.nix
config this tree's flake shell generates.

fix(onchain): restore the carriage-wire golden test's on-chain type names

The generator re-run during the validation-machine split wrote this golden
with `FieldCarriage`/`FieldView`/`FieldPreimageCertificate*` in place of
the on-chain `…V1` type names, and the split commit carried that copy.
Restore the committed bytes; the generator's `--check` and the module's
Aiken tests pass against them.

refactor(onchain): split validation-machine-v1.ak by machine phase

`lib/midgard/validation-machine-v1.ak` was 19,151 lines and 543 top-level
items. It is now `lib/midgard/validation-machine/`, layered so the modules
form a DAG:

- `machine-types`: every witness, control, proof, and evidence type.
- `witness`: witness and control encoders, decoders, well-formedness and
  boundness checks, empties, and hashes.
- `shared`: the validation context, min-ADA rule, structural transition and
  successor helpers, size constants, and the signer-set helpers.
- one module per phase: `canonical-decode`, `input-sets`, `static-rules`,
  `signatures`, `phase-a-native-scripts`, `phase-a-script-preconditions`,
  `resolve-inputs`, `script-sources` (with `-early-stages`,
  `-middle-stages`, `-late-stages` for stages 0-12), `native-scripts`,
  `script-integrity`, `cek`, `value-and-mint`, `ledger-delta`.
- `one-step`: the per-phase one-step and semantics entry points.

Item text is unchanged; 118 private items became `pub` because a phase now
reaches them across a module boundary. The 148 consumer modules import the
new modules under `vm_<module>` aliases. Blueprint identity: every one of
the 805 validators' `compiledCode` is byte-identical to the previous build
(reordering and re-homing functions does not move a single hash); only the
22 `definitions` keys of the machine's types follow the defining module,
and the three tests, one fixture generator, and evidence pins that name
those keys are updated. `aiken check` passes 3,198 of 3,198 tests on the
split tree; the build's 57 warnings are the pre-existing set.

build(hooks): track the git hooks as executable

`.githooks/install`, `pre-commit`, and `post-commit` were tracked with
mode 100644; on a clone (or after any checkout that rewrites them) git
ignores them as non-executable and every commit skips the formatter and
linter the hook exists to run. Track them as 100755.
